title: Industry Pulse — AI / Agent Ecosystem

bullets.title: Claude for Government in public beta — Claude Code + Cowork inside FedRAMP High, tamper-evident audit logs, ATO docs, $1/agency through August
bullets.summary: The same desktop agent stack The Construct runs, now packaged with the security, spend, and audit controls regulated buyers require, deployable via agency MDM with no separate cloud contract.
bullets.how: PRAGMA's regulated-client wedge: our operator hierarchies become sellable into government and compliance-bound enterprises the moment they sit inside a FedRAMP-High, tamper-evident-audited shell — governance and provenance become the product, not the tools.

bullets.title: Claude Opus 5 still the newest frontier weight (Jul 24) — matches/beats Fable 5 at half price, record ARC-AGI-3 jump to 30.2%, outright OSWorld 2.0 computer-use lead
bullets.summary: $5/$25 per 1M (same as Opus 4.8), default on Max and strongest on Pro, clearing Fable 5's peak computer-use score on roughly a third of the budget.
bullets.how: The model to default The Construct's computer-use and agentic-terminal operators onto: frontier-class task-learning and OSWorld performance at half the top-tier cost improves the browser/desktop-driving operators (Pulse, Hermes, the visibility scans) with no pricing hit.

bullets.title: MCP crosses 10,000+ servers as all five majors ship the stateless 2026-07-28 spec — servers now run in a bare Worker with no session infrastructure
bullets.summary: The biggest spec update since 2024 makes MCP stateless with auth hardening and a formal extensions framework; Bedrock AgentCore already hosts it on standard scalable infra.
bullets.how: The substrate we build on just got cheaper and more portable to host: rebuild internal servers on the stateless 2.0 spec so client-facing operators deploy as disposable, horizontally-scalable Workers behind hardened auth — no stateful boxes to babysit.

bullets.title: Reka raises $110M Series B (Snowflake + Nvidia, ~$1B valuation, Jul 22) — a fresh, well-capitalized efficient-model lab
bullets.summary: Another independent lab funded to push cheap-capable models, with strategic infra (Snowflake data, Nvidia compute) behind it.
bullets.how: Reinforces the model-portability thesis: keep operators model-agnostic so we route high-volume, low-stakes steps to whichever efficient lab (Reka, Flash, Luna) wins on cost-per-token while reserving Opus 5 for hard reasoning/computer-use jobs.

bullets.title: arXiv 'Design and Implementation of Agentic Orchestrations and Orchestration of Agents' (2606.31518) — classification framework: task specificity, traceability/tractability, autonomy/reactivity, correctness assurance
bullets.summary: Separates orchestrating agentic steps from orchestrating whole agents and gives named axes to reason about each.
bullets.how: A design vocabulary for our operator hierarchies: score each operator on traceability and correctness-assurance up front to know which jobs run fully autonomous vs. need a human gate — the same governance spine that makes the regulated-deployment wedge (item 1) sellable.

praxis_lesson: Frontier held again today (Opus 5 Jul 24 still newest, GPT-5.6 and Gemini 3.6 Flash unchanged), so the day's real signal is that the whole stack is hardening toward governed, portable deployment — Claude for Government wraps the exact agent stack we run in a FedRAMP-High, tamper-evident-audited shell, MCP goes stateless-and-hosted-anywhere at 10,000+ servers, and fresh capital (Reka) keeps the efficient-model tier competitive. The Construct's edge compounds in the same direction: build model-agnostic operators on the stateless 2.0 spec, score each on traceability and correctness up front, and the same hierarchy sells into a signage SMB and a federal agency alike — governance and provenance are the product while weights and tools commoditize beneath it.
